_note: Byte-for-byte signed-output vectors, verified against real on-device Trust Wallet Core 4.1.19 (the pinned version), via the Android instrumented test SigningConformanceTest.kt, run 2026-08-27 on an emulator. Every vector calls ChainSigner.sign() — the exact code path ChainberryTrustWalletCoreModule.kt uses in production — with a fixed, deterministic (but not necessarily broadcast-valid: fake txids/blockhash/etc.) unsignedTx. Companion to conformance/address-derivation-vectors.json (same test mnemonic/empty passphrase). bitcoincash is absent — sending is unsupported on both platforms (derivation-only, see that fixture). This pass verified Android only; see address-derivation-vectors.json's _note and README.md's Security model section for the iOS gap.

signingVectors._note: Legacy gasPriceHex path in signEvm (as opposed to polygon's EIP-1559 path below) — self-send of 1 ETH to the wallet's own address, fixed nonce/gas.

EIP-1559 maxFeePerGasHex/maxPriorityFeePerGasHex path in signEvm — a genuinely different branch from ethereum's legacy path above, worth its own vector. bnb needs no separate vector: same CoinType/code path as ethereum (see address-derivation-vectors.json).

Self-send: toAddress/changeAddress are the wallet's own bitcoin address (see address-derivation-vectors.json). scriptPubKeyHex was computed via BitcoinScript.lockScriptForAddress() on-device (see SigningConformanceTest.kt) rather than hand-derived from bech32, so it's guaranteed to match this wallet's real P2WPKH lock script. txIdHex/vout/amounts are fixed and NOT a real UTXO — never broadcast this.
Same shape/code path as bitcoin (signUtxo), different CoinType/address — self-send to the wallet's own litecoin address.
Self-send: Account and Destination are both the wallet's own xrp address.

NOT byte-reproducible: signTon() embeds a wall-clock expireAt = now + 600s into the signed BOC, so both the output and meta.txHash (which hashes the BOC) differ every run — confirmed by harvesting this vector twice and getting two different, both-valid outputs. There is deliberately no expectedSignedTx/expectedMeta here; SigningConformanceTest.kt's tonVectorIsWellFormed() instead checks that signing succeeds, the output looks like a well-formed BOC ('te6cc...' prefix), and meta.txHash is present with the right length. This is a real constraint of the production signing code, not a gap in this fixture.

signTron() signs the raw txID digest directly (direct-sign path) and reassembles {...originalTx, signature} in app code — see ChainSigning.kt's signTron doc comment. IMPORTANT DISCOVERY: an all-zero 32-byte digest degenerates silently to an EMPTY signature (no error thrown) in this path — this fixture deliberately uses a non-trivial fake digest instead to get a real signature; do not 'simplify' this back to an all-zero txID. iOS DIVERGENCE, NOT RESOLVED IN THIS PASS (no Swift toolchain available): iOS's signTron sets TronSigningInput.rawJson to the full unsigned tx and returns wallet-core's own output.json reconstruction, instead of Android's txId-only input + manual JSON reassembly. Before this vector can be treated as verified cross-platform, an iOS engineer must run this exact unsignedTx (mnemonic/passphrase above) through the iOS path and confirm the embedded signature hex matches Android's expectedSignedTx's signature field exactly (same digest+key -> same signature is non-negotiable; a mismatch is a real bug) and that the resulting JSON is still consumable by tronWeb.trx.sendRawTransaction.

unsignedTxBase64 was generated with @solana/web3.js (Node, one-off script — see this file's git history/PR description for how): feePayer/from = this wallet's own solana address, to = the System Program id (32 zero bytes, a fixed valid pubkey used purely as a deterministic recipient), recentBlockhash = the same all-zero value (never broadcast, only needs to be shape-valid base58 for wallet-core's TransactionDecoder). signSolana() round-trips this through SolanaTransaction.updateBlockhashAndSign with the same blockhash (see ChainSigning.kt doc comment) — no fresher blockhash is available or needed for a non-broadcast conformance check.
